subject: paper:bijlenga-2017
quote: Adults with ADHD had more autistic symptoms, and they had both more hyper- and hyposensitivity compared to norm groups.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). Establishes the bidirectional (hyper and hypo) sensory atypicality in adult ADHD relative to norms — the content of the mechanism.

subject: paper:bijlenga-2017
quote: Atypical sensory profiles as core features of adult ADHD, irrespective of autistic symptoms
rationale: Verbatim article title. States the study's central conclusion that sensory atypicality is a feature of adult ADHD independent of autistic symptoms, not merely autism comorbidity.

subject: paper:ghanizadeh-2011
quote: Sensory processing problems in children with ADHD are more common than in typically developing children.
rationale: Verbatim from the open-access Psychiatry Investigation abstract (PMC3149116). Systematic-review conclusion that sensory problems are elevated in ADHD children versus controls.

subject: paper:ghanizadeh-2011
quote: Sensory processing problems in children with ADHD is not a well studied area.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. The honest counterweight: the evidence base is thin, so treating sensory difficulty as an established ADHD phenotype feature is premature.

subject: paper:panagiotidi-2018
quote: Results showed a highly significant positive correlation between the number of ADHD traits and the frequency of reported sensory processing problems.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. General-population evidence that sensory difficulty scales with ADHD-trait level — the dimensional strand.

subject: paper:panagiotidi-2018
quote: Our results suggest that sensory difficulties could be part of the ADHD phenotype.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Proposes sensory difficulty as part of the ADHD phenotype; medium confidence given the tentative 'could be' and the questionnaire, general-population design.
